text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'inference-prod' (P1). Multiple pages to ops-contractors service. Incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-89271 — auto-escalation in progress.

Alex P: seeing a flood of pages to ops-contractors instead of our on-call. Are they tagged as fallback?

Maria G: I think the night rotation tag got applied to the wrong service during the config sync. Not the usual ops-oncall target.

Sam H: can someone confirm impact? metrics look like increased 500/502s for hosted generation (us-east-1). Frontend timeouts for customer calls.

pagerbot: 3 pages sent to ops-contractors (rotation id: rot-44). 1st page: 1719000002, 2nd: 1719000010, 3rd: 1719000018. No acks yet.

Alex P: pinging Jordan (currently scheduled) — Jordan T are you up?

Jordan T: I'm on a delayed handoff, got the page but it routed to contractors first. I can jump in in 5. If contractors don't ack, escalate to me.

Ops-SRE: contractors are marking as 'can't access infra' — they don't have access to the private route. So pages are noise and not actionable.

Maria G: ok, immediate mitigation: re-route pagerduty binding to ops-oncall and mute contractors rotation for the next 15m. Sam, can you do a quick override?

Sam H: doing a PD routing override now. Will update config and confirm.

Sam H: quick commands I'm running:
```
# temporary PD routing override to prevent contractor paging
pdctl routing update --service inference-prod --set-target ops-oncall
pdctl rotation mute --rotation rot-44 --duration 15m
```

Sam H: override applied. New pages should go to ops-oncall. Please confirm.

pagerbot: Acknowledgement: routing change received. Next page attempt routed to ops-oncall.

Jordan T: got it, acked and triaging the backend errors now — looks like a cache invalidation job errored and flooded the inference runtime with cold-starts. Working on rolling a hotfix (retry+backoff) to the cache worker.

Alex P: thanks. Can we also disable noisy alert rule that triggers on transient 5xx spikes (right now severity threshold too low)? We should keep SLO alerts but reduce fanout.

Maria G: agreed — lowering alert sensitivity and adding an automatic fallback policy to route to a secondary oncall team (ops-sre) instead of contractors. I'll file the followup.

Ops-SRE: temporary scaling applied to inference-prod pool to absorb load. Error rate coming down from 7% -> 1.2% over last 6m.

pagerbot: Incident PD-89271 acknowledged by Jordan T at 1719000200.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to 'stabilizing'. No customer escalations reported so far, but there were user-visible timeouts for ~12 minutes. Logged in the incident timeline.

Alex P: brief customer impact note: 3rd-party integrations experienced increased latency and occasional 502s for ~10–15 minutes in us-east-1. No data loss. Follow-up: update runbook to prevent contractor rotations being present in production fallbacks.

Maria G: assigning postmortem to Alex P. Action items: (1) fix tag sync script to avoid applying 'night' tags to contractor services, (2) add verification gate on PD routing changes, (3) change default fallback to ops-sre.

Sam H: filed PD config PR: https://git.company/pd-config/pull/451 — includes routing guard and tests.

Jordan T: resolving incident in PD now, will keep monitoring for 30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident PD-89271 resolved at 1719001800.

Maria G: post-incident note: contractors were paged but couldn't take action — this is a breach of our paging policy. We'll follow up with a doc update and a runbook readout next week. :memo:
